References
WebGL

WebGL and extensions

JSAR implements the WebGL (opens in a new tab) and WebGL 2.0 (opens in a new tab) standards, and also provides some WebGL extensions to enhance the graphics rendering capabilities. Here you can find the references about the WebGL and WebGL extensions that JSAR supports.

Convention

In this document, we will use the following convention to describe implementation status:

CodeDescription
NINot Implemented
PIPartially Implemented
YIYet to be Implemented

WebGL APIs

In this section, we will provide the implementation status of the WebGL APIs in JSAR.

Class WebGLRenderingContext

The WebGLRenderingContext interface provides the WebGL rendering context for the drawing surface. It is part of the WebGL API and is used to draw graphics on the scene.

Constants

All the constants defined in the WebGLRenderingContext (opens in a new tab) interface are supported in JSAR, see the MDN's WebGL constants (opens in a new tab) page for more details.

The WebGL context

The following properties and methods provide general information and functionality to deal with the WebGL context:

WebGLRenderingContext.canvas (opens in a new tab)

A read-only back-reference to the HTMLCanvasElement. Might be null if it is not associated with a <canvas> element.

WebGLRenderingContext.drawingBufferWidth (opens in a new tab)

The read-only width of the current drawing buffer. Should match the width of the canvas element associated with this context.

WebGLRenderingContext.drawingBufferHeight (opens in a new tab)

The read-only height of the current drawing buffer. Should match the height of the canvas element associated with this context.

WebGLRenderingContext.getContextAttributes() (opens in a new tab)

Returns a WebGLContextAttributes object containing the actual context configuration.

PropertyDescription
alphaA Boolean that indicates whether the canvas contains an alpha buffer.
depthA Boolean that indicates whether the drawing buffer has a depth buffer of at least 16 bits.
stencilA Boolean that indicates whether the drawing buffer has a stencil buffer of at least 8 bits.
antialiasA Boolean that indicates whether the drawing buffer is antialiased.
failIfMajorPerformanceCaveatA Boolean that indicates whether a context will be created if the system performance is low.
premultipliedAlphaA Boolean that indicates whether the page compositor will assume the drawing buffer contains colors with premultiplied alpha.
preserveDrawingBufferA Boolean that indicates whether the drawing buffer is preserved after rendering.
powerPreferenceA string that indicates the preferred GPU to use.
xrCompatibleA Boolean that indicates whether the context is compatible with the WebXR Device API.

WebGLRenderingContext.isContextLost() (opens in a new tab) (NI)

Returns a Boolean indicating whether the WebGL context has been lost.

WebGLRenderingContext.makeXRCompatible() (opens in a new tab)

Ensures the context is compatible with the user's XR hardware.

At JSAR, you don't need to call this method on the navigator.gl object, because this context is created for XR by default.

Viewing and clipping

WebGLRenderingContext.viewport() (opens in a new tab)

Sets the viewport.

State information

WebGLRenderingContext.activeTexture() (opens in a new tab)

Selects the active texture unit.

WebGLRenderingContext.blendColor() (opens in a new tab)

Sets the blend color.

WebGLRenderingContext.blendEquation() (opens in a new tab)

Sets both the RGB blend equation and alpha blend equation to a single equation.

WebGLRenderingContext.blendEquationSeparate() (opens in a new tab)

Sets the RGB blend equation and alpha blend equation separately.

WebGLRenderingContext.blendFunc() (opens in a new tab)

Sets the source and destination blending factors.

WebGLRenderingContext.blendFuncSeparate() (opens in a new tab)

Sets the source and destination blending factors separately for RGB and alpha.

WebGLRenderingContext.clearColor() (opens in a new tab)

Sets the color to clear the color buffer to.

Note that because the JSAR is a mixed-rendering architecture, to avoid the applications clearing the color buffer, the clearColor won't have any effect.

WebGLRenderingContext.clearDepth() (opens in a new tab)

Sets the value to clear the depth buffer to.

See the note in clearColor, the clearDepth won't have any effect, either.

WebGLRenderingContext.clearStencil() (opens in a new tab)

Sets the value to clear the stencil buffer to.

See the note in clearColor, the clearStencil won't have any effect, either.

WebGLRenderingContext.colorMask() (opens in a new tab)

Sets which color components to write to the color buffer.

WebGLRenderingContext.cullFace() (opens in a new tab)

Specifies whether or not front- and/or back-facing polygons can be culled.

WebGLRenderingContext.depthFunc() (opens in a new tab)

Specifies the function used to compare the depth value of a fragment with the depth buffer.

WebGLRenderingContext.depthMask() (opens in a new tab)

Sets whether writing into the depth buffer is enabled or disabled.

WebGLRenderingContext.depthRange() (opens in a new tab)

Specifies a linear mapping of the depth values in the depth buffer.

WebGLRenderingContext.disable() (opens in a new tab)

Disables a GL capability.

WebGLRenderingContext.enable() (opens in a new tab)

Enables a GL capability.

WebGLRenderingContext.frontFace() (opens in a new tab)

Specifies whether front- or back-facing polygons can be culled.

WebGLRenderingContext.getParameter() (opens in a new tab)

Returns the value of a parameter for a given target.

WebGLRenderingContext.getError() (opens in a new tab)

Returns the error value.

WebGLRenderingContext.hint() (opens in a new tab)

Specifies implementation-specific hints.

WebGLRenderingContext.isEnabled() (opens in a new tab) (NI)

Returns whether a GL capability is enabled or not.

WebGLRenderingContext.lineWidth() (opens in a new tab)

Sets the width of rasterized lines.

WebGLRenderingContext.pixelStorei() (opens in a new tab)

Sets the pixel storage modes.

WebGLRenderingContext.polygonOffset() (opens in a new tab)

Sets the scale and units used to calculate depth values.

WebGLRenderingContext.sampleCoverage() (opens in a new tab) (NI)

Specifies multisample coverage parameters.

WebGLRenderingContext.stencilFunc() (opens in a new tab)

Sets the front and back function and reference value for stencil testing.

WebGLRenderingContext.stencilFuncSeparate() (opens in a new tab)

Sets the front and back function and reference value for stencil testing.

WebGLRenderingContext.stencilMask() (opens in a new tab)

Controls the writing of individual bits in the stencil planes.

WebGLRenderingContext.stencilMaskSeparate() (opens in a new tab)

Controls the writing of individual bits in the stencil planes.

WebGLRenderingContext.stencilOp() (opens in a new tab)

Sets the front and back-facing stencil test actions.

WebGLRenderingContext.stencilOpSeparate() (opens in a new tab)

Sets the front and back-facing stencil test actions.

Class WebGL2RenderingContext

The WebGL2RenderingContext (opens in a new tab) interface provides the WebGL 2.0 rendering context for the drawing surface. It is part of the WebGL 2.0 API and is used to draw graphics on the scene.

See the MDN's WebGL constants (opens in a new tab) page.

WebGL2RenderingContext.bufferSubData() (opens in a new tab) (PI)

WebGL2RenderingContext.getBufferSubData() (opens in a new tab) (NI)

WebGL2RenderingContext.invalidateSubFramebuffer() (opens in a new tab) (NI)

Supported WebGL extensions

In this section, we list the supported WebGL extensions in the JSAR.

EXT_color_buffer_float

See: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/EXT_color_buffer_float (opens in a new tab).

EXT_texture_filter_anisotropic

See: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/EXT_texture_filter_anisotropic (opens in a new tab).

This extension added new constants:

const texture = gl.createTexture();
gl.bindTexture(gl.TEXTURE_2D, texture);
 
const ext = gl.getExtension('EXT_texture_filter_anisotropic');
if (ext) {
  const max = gl.getParameter(ext.MAX_TEXTURE_MAX_ANISOTROPY_EXT);
  gl.texParameterf(gl.TEXTURE_2D, ext.TEXTURE_MAX_ANISOTROPY_EXT, max);
}

OVR_multiview2

See: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/OVR_multiview2 (opens in a new tab).

This extension is used to render to multiple views in a single draw call.

There are new constants added.

  • FRAMEBUFFER_ATTACHMENT_TEXTURE_NUM_VIEWS_OVR: Number of views of the framebuffer object attachment.
  • FRAMEBUFFER_ATTACHMENT_TEXTURE_BASE_VIEW_INDEX_OVR: Base view index of the framebuffer object attachment.
  • MAX_VIEWS_OVR: The maximum number of views. Most VR headsets have two views, but there are prototypes of headset with ultra-wide FOV using 4 views which is currently the maximum number of views supported by multiview.
  • FRAMEBUFFER_INCOMPLETE_VIEW_TARGETS_OVR: If baseViewIndex is not the same for all framebuffer attachment points where the value of FRAMEBUFFER_ATTACHMENT_OBJECT_TYPE is not NONE, the framebuffer is considered incomplete. Calling checkFramebufferStatus for a framebuffer in this state returns FRAMEBUFFER_INCOMPLETE_VIEW_TARGETS_OVR.

This extension also exposes a new method framebufferTextureMultiviewOVR that is used to attach a texture array to the given framebuffer object. However in JSAR, 3D libraries doesn't need to use this function to create a multiview framebuffer. Instead, the application will use the framebuffer that created by the host, and the library will render to the views of the framebuffer.

To make the existing libraries like Three.js or Babylon.js which multiview rendering are still using framebufferTextureMultiviewOVR(), JSAR implemented this function but nothing will happen when it is called.

OCULUS_multiview

This extension is introduced by Meta Horizon (opens in a new tab) at its blog: Multiview WebGL Rendering (opens in a new tab).

This extension inherits from OVR_multiview2 and add a new function framebufferTextureMultisampleMultiviewOVR to address the multisampled antialiasing issue in multiview rendering.

Because of JSAR's mixed-rendering architecture, the multiview framebuffer is managed by the host application, so the library doesn't need to use the function framebufferTextureMultisampleMultiviewOVR to enable multisampled antialiasing in multiview rendering.

To 3D libraries in JSAR, using OCULUS_multiview is the same as using OVR_multiview2, and the library only needs to make draw calls on the multiview framebuffer.
